name: LiteLLM multi-provider gateway
short_definition: Centralize multi-provider LLM access behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway so FastAPI services call one base_url with virtual keys, budgets, routing, retries, and spend tracking. LiteLLM (SDK + Proxy Server) is the default Python-native option as of 2026-07-13 (PyPI litellm 1.92.0). Use the Proxy as the team gateway; use the SDK only for process-local unification without central auth/spend. At extreme RPS, evaluate Go/Envoy gateways (Bifrost, WSO2, etc.) — not default for most product stacks.
scope_in: LiteLLM Proxy (AI Gateway) deployment and config.yaml model_list
LiteLLM Python SDK completion/acompletion vs proxy
Virtual keys, budgets, rate limits, fallbacks/router
OpenAI-compatible client usage from FastAPI (openai SDK or httpx)
When to replace or complement with non-Python gateways
scope_out: Frontend Vercel AI Gateway as sole multi-tenant enterprise control plane (optional complement only)

defaults.mode: Deploy LiteLLM Proxy as internal service (Docker/K8s); apps point openai base_url at proxy
defaults.sdk_when: Single service, few providers, no need for virtual keys/central spend — litellm.acompletion in-process OK
defaults.auth: Proxy master_key + virtual keys per service/team; never share provider master keys to apps
defaults.config: model_list in litellm_config.yaml; secrets via env (os.environ/KEY refs)
defaults.routing: Router fallbacks across Azure/OpenAI/Anthropic deployments for reliability
defaults.budgets: Per-key/project spend limits and RPM/TPM where available
defaults.obs: success_callback to Langfuse/OTel; log model, tokens, cost, request_id — redact content in prod if policy requires
defaults.timeouts: Explicit client timeouts; proxy timeouts aligned with max generation

use_proxy_when: Need virtual keys, spend, central guardrails
Want one OpenAI-compatible URL for all models
use_sdk_only_when: One app, low ops overhead, secrets already isolated
consider_non_python_gateway_when: Measured GIL/latency issues at multi-k RPS on the gateway hop
Org standardizes on Envoy/Go AI gateway with existing ops
do_not: Don't put provider API keys in every microservice
Don't expose LiteLLM proxy to the public internet without auth and network policy
Don't use gateway as a substitute for app-level prompt/authZ checks

do: Run proxy with config as code; pin image tag
Issue per-service virtual keys with least privilege models
Configure fallbacks for primary model outages
Propagate user/project metadata for spend attribution
Monitor proxy latency, error rate, DB log growth
dont: Don't commit master_key or provider keys
Don't unbounded database logging without retention
Don't call 10 providers without timeouts/circuit breakers
Don't dual-write conflicting router logic in every app and the proxy
Don't assume Enterprise SSO features without checking license

# litellm_settings:
#   master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
#   # database_url: os.environ/LITELLM_DATABASE_URL  # for spend/virtual keys

# docker run -v $PWD/litellm_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml -p 4000:4000 \
#   -e OPENAI_API_KEY -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY \
#   docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:main-latest --config /app/config.yaml

# --- FastAPI consumer ---
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    llm_base_url: str = "http://litellm:4000"
    llm_api_key: str  # virtual key
    llm_model: str = "chat-primary"

settings = Settings()  # type: ignore[call-arg]
client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=settings.llm_base_url, api_key=settings.llm_api_key)

async def complete(prompt: str) -> str:
    resp = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model=settings.llm_model,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        timeout=60.0,
    )
    return resp.choices[0].message.content or ""

# --- In-process SDK alternative ---
# from litellm import acompletion
# await acompletion(model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", messages=[...])
failure_modes: Proxy becomes SPOF without HA/replicas and health checks
Spend DB/log table growth degrades request latency (known LiteLLM scaling pain)
Misconfigured model_name aliases → silent wrong model / cost spike
Virtual key leak = billable access to all routed providers
Fallback storms amplify load during provider outage
Python GIL/latency under extreme concurrent streaming fan-out
Enterprise-only features assumed available in OSS proxy
anti_patterns: Every microservice embeds raw OPENAI_API_KEY + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Using proxy for non-LLM CRUD traffic
Ignoring cost attribution (one shared key for all users)
Pinning :latest image in production without digest

versions_as_of.note: Pin litellm image digest in deploy; OSS vs Enterprise feature split for SSO/RBAC

deprecation_watch: Hardcoding provider-specific SDKs in every service without a gateway plan at multi-service scale
LiteLLM as public edge without WAF/auth
Relying solely on in-process SDK when finance needs centralized spend
ts_boundary: Next can call the same OpenAI-compatible proxy with server-side key (Route Handler only). Prefer Python AI service as the product-facing AI API; TS should not hold provider master keys. Vercel AI Gateway is an alternative for TS-centric apps — if Python owns RAG, still route completions via internal LiteLLM or Python service.
rust_boundary: If gateway hop is the bottleneck at high RPS, evaluate Go/Envoy AI gateways; keep Python services as clients of whatever gateway. Do not rewrite app orchestration in Rust just to avoid LiteLLM.
supabase_boundary: Store spend mirrors or usage ledgers in Postgres if product billing needs it; LiteLLM's own DB is ops-facing. Never put provider keys in Supabase client config. Optional: log request_id to messages table for support.
boundary_contracts: Virtual key auth header Authorization: Bearer
Model alias names stable in config (chat-primary)
Env LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL for apps
Optional metadata headers for user/project spend tags

decision_matrix_row.python: LiteLLM Proxy default; SDK for single-app; app uses AsyncOpenAI base_url
decision_matrix_row.ts: Server-only OpenAI client to same proxy or call Python AI service
decision_matrix_row.rust: Only if replacing gateway hop for performance/ops standards

threats: SSRF if proxy can be pointed at internal URLs via malicious model config
Privilege escalation via overly broad master_key distribution
Supply-chain risk on litellm dependency (large surface)
mitigations: Network-isolate proxy; mTLS or private mesh
Rotate virtual keys; least-privilege model allowlists
Separate master_key from app keys; secrets in vault/1Password
uv lock + version pin; monitor CVEs
